TITLE: Install ZarinPal Node.js SDK
DESCRIPTION: Installs the ZarinPal Node.js SDK using npm. This is the primary method for adding the SDK to your Node.js project.


TITLE: ZarinPal Node.js SDK API Reference
DESCRIPTION: Provides a summary of the core API methods available in the ZarinPal Node.js SDK for managing payments, verifications, inquiries, refunds, and reversals.

SOURCE: https://github.com/zarinpal/zarinpal-node-sdk/blob/main/README.md#_snippet_1

LANGUAGE: APIDOC
CODE:
```
ZarinPal SDK API:

Payments:
  create(data): Creates a new payment request.
  getRedirectUrl(authority): Retrieves the payment gateway redirect URL using the authority token.

Fee Calculation:
  feeCalculation(data): Calculates the transaction fee for a given payment.

Verifications:
  verify(data): Verifies the status of a payment transaction.

Inquiries:
  inquire(data): Inquires about the details of a specific transaction.

Refunds:
  create(data): Initiates a refund for a completed transaction.

Reversals:
  reverse(data): Reverses a transaction, typically before settlement.

Unverified Payments:
  list(): Retrieves a list of payments that have not yet been verified.
```

Yes. This backend already supports session-based OAuth with Appwrite, and I’ve added generic endpoints so you can use Google and GitHub.

How it works
- Start flow:
  - POST `/api/auth/oauth/:provider/start` with `{ successUrl, failureUrl }`
  - Returns a redirect URL to the provider via Appwrite.
- Callback:
  - Appwrite posts back `userId` and `secret` to your backend callback.
  - POST `/api/auth/oauth/:provider/callback` with `{ userId, secret }`
  - Backend creates an Appwrite session from `userId, secret`, sets cookies, ensures profile, and redirects to your frontend (session-based).
- Session usage:
  - GET `/api/auth/oauth/me` reads the `appwrite_session` cookie and returns the current user.
  - POST `/api/auth/oauth/logout` clears cookies (session-based logout).

What you need to enable
- In Appwrite: enable Google and GitHub OAuth providers and configure the callback URLs to your backend, e.g. `https://yourdomain.com/api/auth/oauth/google/callback` and `/api/auth/oauth/github/callback`.
- Frontend: call start endpoint, then redirect user to the URL it returns. Point provider callback to your backend endpoints above.

Notes
- No Passport is required; this uses Appwrite sessions.
- If you already use the GitHub-specific endpoints, the new generic routes allow the same flow for Google without code duplication.

- Backend route `/api/site-config/current` reads from Appwrite and defaults to normal if unavailable. Since your frontend cannot reach the Nest API (timeout), query Appwrite directly as a fallback.

Minimal frontend fallback (using Appwrite Web SDK)
- Install and initialize Appwrite client in the frontend.
- Query the site_config collection for the latest doc.

Example:
```javascript
import { Client, Databases, Query } from 'appwrite';

const client = new Client()
  .setEndpoint('https://your-appwrite-endpoint/v1')
  .setProject('YOUR_PROJECT_ID');

const databases = new Databases(client);

export async function fetchSiteModeFallback() {
  try {
    const databaseId = 'YOUR_DATABASE_ID';
    const collectionId = 'site_config'; // or the actual ID in env

    const res = await databases.listDocuments(databaseId, collectionId, [
      Query.orderDesc('created_at'),
      Query.limit(1),
    ]);

    const doc = res.documents?.[0];
    return { success: true, data: { mode: doc?.mode || 'normal' } };
  } catch (e) {
    return { success: true, data: { mode: 'normal' } };
  }
}
```

Notes
- This mirrors backend logic in `src/site-config/site-config.service.ts` (order by `created_at` desc and limit 1; fallback to normal).
- Keep backend as the primary source; use this only when `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/site-config/current` is unreachable.
- Your current backend endpoint returns normal mode successfully when reachable: see `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/site-config/current`.
